scope: Moves only miss code into the existing async disk subroutine or new noinline synchronous helper. No mask, cold annotation, diagnostic, cache protocol or public API changes.
correctness_review: Sync initial lookup/bounds validation and resident hit path remain unchanged. Only an unmapped directory result calls the new helper.

Sync helper preserves allocator validation for both blocking and nonblocking requests. Invalid returns FALSE/BAD_PARAM, valid nonblocking miss returns FALSE/BUSY, blocking delegates to existing disk loader and preserves its retry flag.
An admission race returns TRUE from disk helper, causing outer synchronous get to repeat full lookup and revalidate membership only if still unmapped.

Async async_begin(state, depth) resumes by jumping to a previously saved label; initial allocation validation occurs once before entry acquisition. On I/O resumption it is skipped, as it was previously skipped by outer state resumption.

Moving validation across async_await_subroutine initialization introduces no actual yield or callback between validation and entry acquisition. The initial child call executes inline in the same stack before its first await.

Invalid async input sets BAD_PARAM and succeeded TRUE, marks child DONE, propagates DONE through internal child and top-level state. No cache reference, I/O state, queue insertion, callback or entry reservation occurs.

When entry acquisition races with another loader, succeeded FALSE causes the top-level retry. async_await_subroutine initializes inner child states again, so a repeated miss repeats allocation validation.
The cache extent lifetime and existing race/identity recheck protocol is unchanged. This does not repair or claim to repair the separate inherited batch reservation progress limitation.
validation: Source review only; root owns build, codegen check, correctness tests and benchmarks. The actual invalid-address worktree remains untouched.
